subject: Interim capacity bridge plan for Helix deal (US/EU/APAC sizing)
messages:
From: Jin Park <jin.park@helix.ai>
To: connor.obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@helix.ai, sridhar@helix.ai
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 08:32:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: temporary region bridge capacity while contract finalizes

Connor —

Appreciate the demo last week. Helix is ramping faster than we projected and procurement is pushing us to get predictable regional throughput for our customers in US, EU, and APAC before the full contract is signed. Specifically:

- US: steady sustained need ~120 concurrent inferencing sessions (~20 tokens/session avg) during business hours, peak bursts up to ~230.
- EU: steady ~60 concurrent, peaks ~110.
- APAC: smaller base ~30 concurrent, but critical low-latency requirement for Tokyo customers with spikes tied to batch runs.

We know the full Dedicated reserved-capacity SOW will take ~4–6 weeks. In the meantime, can Redwood provide an "interim capacity bridge" (short-term dedicated nodes / reserved burst lanes) for 6–8 weeks so we can avoid customer impact? We need a quick yes/no on feasibility, an estimated node count per region, and a rough cost delta so procurement can approve an emergency PO.

Also attaching our traffic profile and expected ramp csv (attachment: helix-traffic-sept.csv).

Thanks — Jin
Jin Park
Head of Platform
Helix AI

Hi Jin —

Thanks for the context and the traffic file. We can absolutely support an interim bridge but need to confirm a few internal sizing assumptions before I give a firm node count and cost. High level: yes on a 6–8 week short-term reservation (we've done similar bridge plays for two pilots this year).

Internal ask to my ops and pricing partners: can you please look at the attached traffic and provide a recommend node mix (GPU type, quantization profile, and burst lane plan) for US / EU / APAC and a ballpark cost per week?

Karthik and Marissa — please weigh in on whether we should offer a capped-burst SLA (soft 95th pct) or a hard reservation for the bridge. Hannah / Laura — can we feasibly spin the APAC low-latency nodes in Tokyo region in under 10 business days if we provision as "urgent"?

I'll compile the answers into a short proposal and a one-page MOP for Helix procurement.

Connor O'Brien
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference

Quick ops readout after reviewing Jin's profile and the Helix csv:

- Assumptions we used: 20 tokens/sec average per session, 95th pct concurrency factor = 1.7 for spikes, quantized Llama-2.1 70B-ish performance equivalence (most cost-efficient path).
- Recommended short-term node mix (to meet the requested 6–8 week window):
  - US (us-west-2): 6 gpus (A100-80GB equiv) configured in 3-node pool with continuous-batching + prefix caching. Burst lane cap: extra 3 GPUs available as preemptible for short bursts.
  - EU (europe-west-1): 3 gpus (A100-80GB equiv) in 2-node pool, burst lane: +1 preemptible.
  - APAC (asia-northeast-1 / Tokyo): 2 gpus (A10x4-80GB equiv or T4x with low-latency tuning) pinned to low-latency hosts; burst lane: +1.
- Timeline: US/EU provisioning ~4 business days; APAC ~8–9 business days (hardware availability dependent).
- Ops caveat: APAC pinning increases unit cost ~18% due to low-latency hosts.

I'll attach a sizing workbook with node-level assumptions and a short runbook for request routing during the bridge window. Laura — can you get an emergency PO cadence and billing terms for a short-term reserve?

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Regional Ops | Redwood Inference
From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Interim capacity bridge estimate and MOP for Helix

Jin — attaching our short proposal and MOP draft. Summary below and attachment list:  

Summary (6-week bridge, paid weekly):
- US: 6 reserved GPUs + 3 preemptible burst GPUs — estimated cost $62,500/week.
- EU: 3 reserved GPUs + 1 preemptible burst GPU — estimated cost $28,000/week.
- APAC: 2 low-latency pinned GPUs + 1 burst — estimated cost $24,500/week (includes priority placement premium).
- One-time setup & network peering fee: $5,000.
- Total estimated weekly run-rate (all regions): $115,000/week.
- Minimum bridge term we can sign today: 4 weeks; preferred for risk = 6 weeks.

Attachments: 20260909-helix-bridge-sizing-proposal.xlsx (sizing & node assumptions), 20260909-helix-mop-draft.pdf (MOP + routing), invoice-terms-template.docx (billing cadence).

Action items for procurement if you want to proceed quickly:
1) Approve PO for 4 weeks to start (we can extend)
2) Sign the short MOP (one-page) to allow us to prioritize node placement
3) Provide point-of-contact for network peering and certs

If that looks reasonable I'll loop in our provisioning team to begin immediate spin-up once the PO is in.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Revenue Finance | Redwood Inference

Thanks all — this is helpful and faster than I expected. Procurement has green-lit a 4-week emergency PO to get us through the contract finalization. They asked for two small changes before they send the PO:

- Can Redwood convert the one-time setup fee into a refundable credit applied to the first invoice if Helix converts to a full Dedicated contract within 12 weeks?
- Can we get a single consolidated weekly invoice instead of regional invoices?

Both are straightforward for us; if you can confirm we will have the signed PO by Monday EOD and an onboarding contact for peering. Also copying Sridhar who will be the technical lead for peering and cert coordination.

Jin
